claims.text: Rapidly quenched Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 retains a metastable high-temperature BCC structure.
The rapidly quenched alloy has minimal short-range chemical order.
Phase stability in the initial BCC state is governed jointly by a thermodynamic driving force for chemical ordering and sluggish diffusion kinetics.
Localized Cr-Al interactions provide a thermodynamic driving force for chemical ordering.
Local compositional fluctuations favor nucleation of an ordered or alternative phase.
Atomic diffusion below the quench temperature is too slow for the full transformation to occur under standard annealing conditions.
The kinetic barrier from sluggish diffusion allows the BCC phase to persist during annealing.
Sufficient diffusion enables Cr-Al chemical ordering and subsequent phase transformation.
Local Cr-Al ordering and short-range clustering act as precursors to nucleation of an ordered or secondary phase.
Longer isothermal holds at 600-700 °C will increase chemical ordering or secondary-phase formation.
A diffusion-enhancing dopant or processing modification will increase the rate and degree of ordering relative to conventional annealing.
Ordering or secondary-phase formation will produce emerging diffraction features and detectable nanoscale or compositional heterogeneity.
Ordering transformations may produce exothermic DSC peaks.
At sufficiently high temperature, increased atomic mobility eliminates the kinetic barrier that preserves the BCC state.
Segregation or casting defects can dominate transformation behavior outside the proposed boundary conditions.
